study type: Retrospective analysis of prospectively collected data
exposure: Entry method (sheath + trocar; cannula + trocar; cannula + Seldinger)
cohort: The cohort consisted of 673 cases of twin pregnancies with at least one survivor who underwent fetoscopic laser treatment for twin-twin transfusion syndrome.
finding: Access diameter was associated with preterm birth <28 weeks, and cervical length was critically associated with obstetrical outcomes following fetoscopic laser surgery, while entry method did not significantly impact PROM or latency to birth.
